written.myAnswer: In dynamic equilibrium, the forward and reverse reactions continue at equal rates, so concentrations remain constant. In static equilibrium, there is no ongoing change or movement.
Use a catalyst to increase the rates of both the forward and reverse reactions; suitable reaction conditions can also help. This reduces the time needed to reach equilibrium.
The phase changes of water are reversible: melting and freezing reverse one another, as do evaporation and condensation.
Initially, the forward reaction is faster and the backward reaction is slow. As products form, the backward rate increases. At equilibrium, the forward and backward rates are equal.
A catalyst increases the rates of both the forward and backward reactions, so equilibrium is reached sooner; it does not stop either reaction or change the equilibrium position.
